alex_k: on it, pulling logs

jonathan: i'm on pager, taking lead. immediate mitigation: cordon the suspect nodes and drain them (ignore-daemonsets, delete-local-data). also start traffic-steer to other pools per runbook
alex_k: executing: `kubectl cordon infer-node-usw2-07` -> OK
alex_k: `kubectl drain infer-node-usw2-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> evicting pods, some serving replicas rescheduled to other nodes
maya_s: infra: can we shift traffic away from infer-usw-2 to infer-use-1 and infereu-west? errors jump to 9% during spike
infra-bot: initiated traffic shift: 30% -> infereu-west, 40% -> infer-use-1, 30% remain. see runbook: https://docs.redwood/inference/runbooks/node-flap
incidents-bot: Observability: customer-facing error rate reduced 9% -> 3% after partial reroute (p95 latency improved slightly)
jonathan: checking node logs now. `/var/log/messages` and `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` show kernel symbol mismatch and GPU driver crash on kubelet restart — looks like driver got into a bad state after a node restart/rolling kernel update
alex_k: thought: do we taint or cordon + reboot first? prefer cordon + reboot to avoid noisy scheduling churn
jonathan: plan: cordon 07 & 08, drain, schedule reboots sequentially, escalate to eng-runtime for driver rollback if reboots don't stabilize. I'll update severity to P1 for next steps (we stopped immediate customer degradation).
